title: Context and useReducer
summary: Passing data deeply with context, providers and defaults, re-render costs, reducers as pure functions of state and action, and combining the two for app-level state.

sections.title: Context passes data through the tree
sections.body:
Create a context with a default, provide a value high in the tree and read it anywhere below with `useContext` (or `use`). The **default** is used only when there is **no provider above** the reader.

In React 19 you can render the context itself as the provider: `<ThemeContext value="dark">`. `<ThemeContext.Provider value="dark">` still works.

sections.title: Context and re-renders
sections.body:
When a provider's `value` changes (by `Object.is`), **every** component reading that context re-renders, even if it is wrapped in `memo`. Passing a new object literal each render, `value={{ user, setUser }}`, changes the value every time the provider's parent renders. Memoise it with `useMemo`, or split rarely changing and often changing data into separate contexts.

Use context for truly widely needed data (theme, current user, locale, a store). For passing props two or three levels, plain props or composition with `children` are often clearer.

sections.title: useReducer
sections.body:
`const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, initialState)` moves update logic into a **pure** function `reducer(state, action) => nextState`. Handlers describe what happened, `dispatch({ type: "added", item })`, and the reducer decides how state changes. Reducers are easy to unit test because they are plain functions.

A reducer must not mutate state or have side effects (in StrictMode development React calls it twice). Return a new object for changes, and return the same `state` for unknown actions or throw.

sections.title: Reducer plus context
sections.body: A common pattern for app-level state: keep state in `useReducer` at the top, put `state` in one context and `dispatch` in another. `dispatch` is stable for the component's lifetime, so components that only dispatch do not re-render when state changes. Wrap the pair in a provider component and export small hooks such as `useTodos()` that throw a clear error when used outside the provider.

pitfalls: Expecting the default value when a provider exists but passes `undefined`; the provider wins.
Creating a new value object every render and re-rendering every consumer.
Side effects (fetching, logging analytics) inside a reducer.

gotchas.question: What does `Label` render?
gotchas.answer: "default" then "provided". The first `Label` has no provider above it.

gotchas.question: Does `memo` stop a component re-rendering when a context it reads changes?
gotchas.answer: No. `memo` compares props only; a context change always re-renders its readers.
